reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal behavior is a periodic square-wave pulse train with robust-standardized amplitude peaking near 3.0 and baseline at 0.0. Each pulse has near-vertical rise and fall (sharp edges), flat top and bottom, and consistent width (~10–12 points) and spacing (~85–90 points between onsets), yielding an estimated period of ~97 points—matching the catalog’s estimated_period. All candidates show identical amplitude_90 (2.995), zero median/MAD, zero roughness/curvature, confirming stationarity and absence of trend or noise in the standardized space. Pulses are symmetric in shape across cycles; no decay, drift, or jitter is visible. Minor variation exists only in pulse count per window (1P, 3P, 3P, 5P) due to window length scaling, not frequency shift. The pattern is highly stable: all four candidates align morphologically—same height, width, duty cycle (~10–12%), and inter-pulse interval—indicating a deterministic, non-stochastic process. Acceptable variation includes slight timing offsets (<±2 points) in pulse onset across windows, but no amplitude modulation, baseline offset, or distortion. No evidence of contamination: all pulses maintain crisp edges and uniform height; no partial, attenuated, or irregular pulses appear.
